Trace fossils record biological activity rather than a preserved body part. A footprint impression, a burrow, or a coprolite can preserve evidence of an organism.
A mold preserves an impression left by an organism. A cast forms when material fills that cavity, creating a three-dimensional copy of the original shape.
Body fossils preserve actual parts of organisms, such as bones, shells, or plant material. They differ from evidence of activity left without the organism itself.
Entrapment in resin that becomes amber can preserve organisms. Amber preservation is different from filling a bone with minerals; fossils do not all become stone.
